composition.observation: A full-width Personal Information hero introduces a two-column desktop layout with account sections beside the editor. On phone width, a compact sections disclosure precedes the same single-column editor and Return to Home remains in the hero.

hierarchy.observation: The Personal Information heading anchors the page. The display-name field and gold save button are grouped in the first panel, above the separate verified-email change task. The settled Home title and Explore Chronicles are the leading destination cues, but both are temporarily removed by automatic playback.

typography.observation: The serif page and card titles differentiate context from the smaller sans-serif field labels and feedback. On phone width the primary email wraps onto two lines under its own label and the edited display name remains readable in the focused input.

spacing.observation: The desktop panel gutters distinguish the editor from the sidebar. The narrower capture keeps separate rows for Return to Home, the sections disclosure, and the editor, and the added unsaved label enlarges the hero without overlapping adjacent controls.

controls.observation: Return to Home looks like a secondary outlined action close to the account heading. Save display name is a distinct gold action beside the draft task. Home briefly withdraws the visible primary continuation cues while offering presentation controls after arriving.

contrast.observation: Light editor headings, field text and the white focused-input outline stand out against the dark teal surfaces, and the gold primary button reads clearly at both viewport widths. The gateway title and action temporarily lose visible contrast when they fade out in reduced mode.

consistency.observation: The Voyagewright masthead, dark harbor surfaces, gold action accents and signed-in identity remain recognizable between the Personal Harbor and the shared Gateway. The compact navigation fits the phone-width frames while the desktop frame exposes its navigation links.

states.observation: The captured sequence shows the editor with the fixture name, a modified local name and Unsaved changes, and the signed-in Home gateway afterward. Trace frames add an intermediate Home presentation state that the settled screenshots do not represent.

responsive.observation: At 1440 by 900 the editor and section navigation are side by side. At 390 by 844 the navigation compresses into a disclosure, the email wraps, and the label, draft, save button and return affordance remain readable in one column.

keyboard.observation: Both traces activate the named Return to Home link with Enter and reach the signed-in gateway. The focused Return to Home ring is visible before leaving. These Chromium captures establish the keyboard route in both viewport sizes.

focus.observation: After the edit the strong outline remains on Display name alongside Unsaved changes in both screenshots. It moves to the return link before Enter in the traces. The captured contexts stay reduced throughout. Separate browser cases contain the live OS-media switch assertions.

feedback.observation: Unsaved changes appears only in the edited screenshots, alongside the return control and with the draft visibly inside Display name. Save display name remains a separate action and neither trace activates it during the return journey.

motion.observation: Both Chromium traces declare reducedMotion reduce. Desktop first paints Home then hides its content and restores the title and actions about 663 ms after that first paint. Phone width does the same in about 522 ms, with a visible reduced motion label and a transient Skip opening presentation control.

continuity.observation: The editable draft and its feedback survive through the account step and the Creator reaches the signed-in destination using the ordinary route. The first-paint Home heading and action disappear before returning, interrupting the visual handoff.

complexity.observation: A single named field, a local unsaved indicator, and one visible Return to Home link make the account task direct on both viewports. On phone width the automatic gateway presentation introduces a second decision, Skip opening presentation, before the primary action is fully available again.

role-outcomes.observation: The signed-in Creator fixture enters Personal Information, edits the display name as a local draft, sees the explicit unsaved state and reaches Home with the signed-in account marker. The desktop settled gateway includes a Creator continuation card.

fallbacks.observation: Reduced-mode editing and Enter-based return both complete with the ordinary labeled controls, and the gateway eventually exposes the same navigation. Its skip control briefly provides an escape from the opening sequence, while the reduced-mode return itself still withdraws the visible primary task.

findings.observation: With browser reduced motion enabled, edit Display name in Personal Information and activate Return to Home with Enter. Home visibly paints Choose your role in Voyagewright, Explore Chronicles and the start of the role cards, then the automatic gateway presentation removes the heading and key actions before restoring them. Desktop frames 46–55 show the full sequence over about 663 ms from first Home paint. Mobile frames 30–45 show it over about 522 ms, with Skip opening presentation visible during the interruption. This withdraws already-visible destination content during the normal reduced-motion return. The settled state alone conceals the interruption. Matching protected-base runtime behavior was not established.
